content: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) is a government agency in Australia responsible for collecting and publishing statistical data about the country and its population. The ABS conducts the Australian Census of Population and Housing every five years, as mandated by the Census and Statistics Act 1905, Section 8. The most recent census at the time was conducted on August 8, 2006, and the results were made available on the ABS website starting June 27, 2007. Since 1978, the ABS has been conducting surveys to gather data on research and development (R&D) expenditures and human resources dedicated to R&D in Australia. These surveys provide critical information for monitoring the nature and distribution of R&D activities, which is used by government policy analysts, advisors, businesses, and economists. The ABS conducts four specific R&D surveys: 1. The R&D Business Survey, conducted annually. 2. The R&D Higher Education Survey, conducted every two years. 3. The R&D General Government Survey, conducted every two years. 4. The R&D Private Non-Profit Sector Survey, conducted every two years. The ABS reports R&D data using the Australian Standard Research Classification (ASRC). The first ASRC was introduced in 1993 and was used until 1998. It included three classification schemes: Type of Activity (TOA), Field of Research (FOR), and Socio-Economic Objective (SEO). In 1998, a revised ASRC was released, which replaced the Field of Research (FOR) classification with the Research Field, Course, and Discipline (RFCD) classification. This updated classification system was implemented during the 2000 collection period, with data submissions due by August 31, 2001. The Type of Activity (TOA) classification categorizes R&D activities based on the type of research effort, which includes: Pure basic research. Strategic basic research. Applied research. Experimental development. The Research Field, Course, and Discipline (RFCD) classification allows for the categorization of R&D activities and other activities within the higher education sector. It is used to classify courses, units of study, and teaching activities by field. The classification includes recognized academic disciplines, major sub-fields taught at universities or tertiary institutions, research areas investigated by national research organizations, and emerging fields of study. The Socio-Economic Objective (SEO) classification categorizes R&D activities based on their intended purpose, as perceived by the researcher. It includes distinct economic, social, technological, or scientific domains and considers factors such as processes, products, health, education, and other social and environmental aspects. The ABS also publishes an annual reference work called the Year Book Australia. This publication provides a comprehensive statistical overview of various aspects of Australia's economy and social conditions. It also includes descriptive content on topics such as geography, climate, government, international relations, defense, education, and health and welfare systems. The head of the ABS has been referred to as the Australian Statistician since 1975. Prior to this, the position was known as the Commonwealth Statistician. A complete list of individuals who have held this office is available under the title Australian Statistician. As of March 2007, the Australian Statistician was Brian Pink.
